project.description:
Stages the HPDS data named in build-spec.json (of the release-control checkout) into the stack bucket as data/<deploy key>/... Run by hand; Check For Updates does not call this job. It only checks that the data for the current deploy keys is staged and that data/<auth key>/fence_mapping.json exists.
Order of a data release: (1) commit the new source URLs in build-spec.json, (2) run this job with HPDS_VARIANT=both, (3) run Check For Updates (or wait for the scheduled run) to deploy. Rollback: put the old tar URLs back in build-spec.json (that gives a new deploy key), run this job with both, then Check For Updates.
HPDS_VARIANT: both (default) = auth, then open, in one build; a failed auth stops before open. auth -> javabins_rekeyed/ (legacy tar javabins_rekeyed.tar), open -> destigmatized_javabins_rekeyed/ (legacy tar destigmatized_javabins_rekeyed.tar, concepts removed). Per variant the source URL and the deploy key (blame commit of the source_dataset_s3_url / source_destigmatized_dataset_s3_url line) are derived from build-spec.json by the same rules as Check For Updates. A variant that is already staged is skipped ("already staged, skipping"); a staged prefix (manifest.tsv) or tar is never overwritten. data/<auth key>/fence_mapping.json sits outside the stage prefixes and is written by the auth variant only (its metadata.json; for a legacy tar, the metadata.json inside the tar). The open variant never writes it: PSAMA reads the auth key's. When the auth variant is already staged per-file but fence_mapping.json is missing, this job copies data/<auth key>/javabins_rekeyed/metadata.json to it (server-side, SSE-S3), prints "fence_mapping.json restored from the staged metadata.json" and checks that it exists afterwards. An auth variant staged as a legacy tar without fence_mapping.json is refused: restage it under a new deploy key (commit a change to the source URL lines of build-spec.json, then run this job).
Source URL: - ends with .tar: legacy path (assume curated-datasets-s3-role, download, open: RemoveConceptFromMetadata in docker, re-tar, upload). - dataset prefix (ends with /, has manifest.json schema bdc-hpds-pheno-release/1): per-file staging. Each file of the variant is read from the source with curated-datasets-s3-role (an AWS CLI profile in a private temporary config file assumes it; the CLI renews the session, no credential passes through the shell and the profile is used for the source reads only) and streamed through this Jenkins host into the stack bucket with the instance role (SSE-S3, no docker, no Bash_Functions). Before anything is written the job checks that the role can be assumed (sts get-caller-identity) and refuses otherwise. A failure on either side of a copy fails the build. Byte check of every copy against the manifest, the auth variant's metadata.json also copied to fence_mapping.json, manifest.tsv written last. Refuses: unknown variant, bad manifest, open variant with the full columnMeta (stored sha or, when present, the gunzipped content sha of full and open is equal), auth files from open/. A run that died before manifest.tsv can be retried.
IAM for the dataset-prefix path: - the source bucket (bdc-etl-data-d0d6191) is in another account than this Jenkins: the instance role cannot read it. Dataset prefixes are read through curated_datasets_s3_role (arn:aws:iam::515157839325:role/curated-datasets-s3-role by default, the same role as the legacy .tar path): s3:GetObject on data/hpds/pheno/datasets/* of the source bucket. The instance role needs sts:AssumeRole on it, and the trust policy of curated-datasets-s3-role in account 515157839325 must allow the deploy-account instance role. - the source credentials are obtained by the CLI from the instance metadata (credential_source=Ec2InstanceMetadata), so the instance metadata service must be reachable from the Jenkins container, as it already is for every aws call. - the instance role writes and lists the stack bucket (stack_s3_bucket): s3:ListBucket (prefix data/*), s3:GetObject and s3:PutObject on data/* (SSE-S3, no KMS). The source role is never used for the stack bucket. - the data streams through the Jenkins host (download from the source, upload to the stack bucket, one file at a time): allow time and bandwidth for the large files, allObservationsStore.javabin is tens of GB. The legacy .tar path keeps using curated-datasets-s3-role and sources the scripts in the Bash_Functions job workspace (assume_role, reset_role, get_stack); Check For Updates no longer runs Bash_Functions first, so if that workspace is missing, build Bash_Functions once before a legacy run.
DEPLOY_TO_STAGING_STACK (default false): false = stage only; nothing is deployed. A flag-off run can still restore a missing data/<auth key>/fence_mapping.json (auth data staged per-file) or refuse an auth variant that is staged as a legacy tar without one (see above). true = after every requested variant is staged or already staged, a second build step starts HPDS Data - Deploy to Staging Stack (which takes the locks) with the auth, open and genomic deploy keys, and waits for it. That job takes the deployment-state lock and the stack lock, resolves the staging stack (environments.next_prod in deployment_state_metadata/stacks.json), re-checks that the data is staged and deploys, in this order: (1) PIC-SURE HPDS Auth Deploy, (2) PIC-SURE HPDS Open Deploy, (3) PIC-SURE Auth Micro App Deploy. Why PSAMA: it copies data/<auth deploy key>/fence_mapping.json into its container when it starts, so it is redeployed with the dataset. Its description names the locks, the time limit and the IAM it needs. The genomic deploy key is computed as in Check For Updates (blame commit of the source_genomic_dataset_s3_url line). The deploy needs the data of BOTH variants: with HPDS_VARIANT=auth or open the other variant must already be staged for its current deploy key. The build is refused, and the deploy job is not started, when: the other variant is not staged, fence_mapping.json is missing and cannot be restored (auth staged as a legacy tar), or the genomic deploy key is empty or not a git hash. The live stack cannot be targeted from this job: it has no stack parameter and looks up no stack. The deploy job is started only from the file the checks write (staging_deploy.properties in the workspace, deleted at the start of every build), which holds the three keys and nothing else. If the deploy job does not end SUCCESS this build fails and names it. Aborting this build only stops its wait: the deploy job it started keeps running (and releases its lock at the end). To stop the deployment, abort the job HPDS Data - Deploy to Staging Stack itself. On success the build prints "Deployed to the staging stack only. A later Deployment Pipeline run rebuilds the staging stack from build-spec.json." (Deployment Pipeline targets the staging stack too; the live stack changes only by a stack swap.) The deploy step is a non-sandboxed system Groovy script that runs on EVERY build (with the flag off it only prints "staging deploy: not requested"). After the job definition is upserted, approve the script under Manage Jenkins, In-process Script Approval, before the first build, whatever the flag is. The last line of the build says either "Deployed to the staging stack only. A later Deployment Pipeline run rebuilds the staging stack from build-spec.json." or "staging deploy: not requested".

hudson.model.ChoiceParameterDefinition.name: HPDS_VARIANT
hudson.model.ChoiceParameterDefinition.description: both stages auth then open; auth stages javabins_rekeyed/, open stages destigmatized_javabins_rekeyed/. Variants that are already staged are skipped.

hudson.model.BooleanParameterDefinition.name: DEPLOY_TO_STAGING_STACK
hudson.model.BooleanParameterDefinition.description: After the requested variants are staged, start HPDS Data - Deploy to Staging Stack (which takes the locks, resolves the staging stack and deploys HPDS auth, HPDS open and PSAMA to it) with the current deploy keys. Needs both variants staged for their current deploy keys and data/<auth key>/fence_mapping.json. Never targets the live stack. Default false: stage only.
